note: Q63 governs the DA params floors and the owner-set drain protection accepted in F04 §4, and pins them in both languages. Acceptance clauses (a) governed lower bounds and (b) owner-set drain protection are implemented in `onchain/aiken/validators/da-params-governor.ak` and measured by the groups below. Acceptance clause (c) — the partial-attestation rescue/refund path — is NOT delivered here: it requires new `MintRedeemer` and `SpendRedeemer` constructors, and both enums live in `onchain/aiken/lib/midgard/da-attestation-types.ak`, which is Q62's exclusive lease and forbidden to this task. The rescue groups are therefore recorded OPEN with their blocker, and this gate exits non-zero until they carry measured evidence. No count here is a declaration count: every published number is recomputed from an executed runner report. Deployment consequence of the F04 §4 floor, recorded so it is not rediscovered in the field: because `max(2, ceil(2*1/3)) == 2 > 1`, a one-member DA committee (and likewise a one-member owner set) is now unrepresentable — there is no `da_threshold` such a committee could name — so every single-signer DA topology is invalid by construction and must move to at least two members.

floorTable.note: Quoting F04's floor text proves the decision record still says what Q63 cited; it does not prove either implementation computes it. This digest is the shared pin that does. The verifier recomputes `max(2, ceil(2n/3))` from an integer ceiling written independently of the `(2n+2)/3` form both implementations use, hashes the table, and asserts this value; the `floor-arithmetic-provenance` Vitest check hashes the table produced by the SDK's `governedThresholdFloor` and asserts the same value. A floor/ceil transcription error on either side breaks one of the two legs.

compiler.rule: Aiken test execution for this goal is fork-only: the stock v1.1.22 build that is the authority for compilation and applied validator hashes ships a codegen defect and takes hours over this tree, so it is used only for `aiken check --skip-tests`. This gate fails closed when `MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN` is unset rather than falling through to whatever `aiken` is first on PATH, and records the spawned binary's self-reported version in its output so a published on-chain result always names the compiler that produced it.

implementation.constantSplit: `min_governed_threshold` bounds a threshold, `min_owner_count` bounds a set size. The off-chain twin mirrors the split as `MIN_DA_GOVERNED_THRESHOLD` and `MIN_DA_OWNER_COUNT` so a change to either cannot silently move the other. The `owner_len >= min_owner_count` check is redundant under the current floor (a one-owner set already fails because `update_threshold` would have to be both >= 2 and <= 1) and is kept as declared defense in depth against a future weakening of the two-thirds term; the drain rejection test is named for the resulting overlap rather than claiming a single disposition.

openGroups.claim: A partially signed attestation stranded by a mid-flight committee rotation can be rescued/refunded.

blockedOn.reason: Recovering the stranded ADA requires burning the DAAT NFT. The burn runs the minting policy, and both `MintRedeemer` constructors (`Init`, `ApplyToStateQueue`) demand a state-queue attachment that a sub-threshold attestation can never satisfy; both `SpendRedeemer` constructors (`AddSignatures`, `BurnForStateQueue`) are equally unusable after rotation because `validate_add_signatures` pins `params.committee_signers_hash` to the datum's. A rescue therefore needs a new constructor in each enum, and both enums are declared in Q62's leased type module.

openGroups.claim: The rescue path rejects theft of another party's attestation value, duplicate refunds, and replay of a consumed rescue.

blockedOn.reason: These rejection classes can only be authored against the rescue redeemer that the lease blocks.
